runtime.command_template: python -B tools/run_pinmame_harness.py --library <working-root>/builds/seawitch-pinned/Release/pinmame64.dll --game seawitch --rom-path <authorized-read-only-ROM-root> --work-dir <new-state-directory> --scenario tools/harness-scenarios/stern/seawitch-<name>.json --output <external-run.json>. No keyboard handling, mechanics mask 0, default binary output mode. The linked official pinned CMake project was path-absolutized in an external project; native-and-rom-identity.json records the source and build hashes.

gameplay.note: Each bumper and sling fires its own coil; the final target of each bank causes its reset; held outhole causes repeat serves/resets, release advances play; tilt drops relay 19. Lower button inputs publish both synthetic outputs of their pair. Lamp 51 changes during this game despite having no printed load; its transition during the upper-button-83 action is background activity and is not evidence that 83 controls it. All four unlisted SCR fitments remain unknown.

self-test.limitation: Burn-in multiplexes digit cycling, so the physical-to-public map is read from this game's own decoder/SCR circuit and corroborated by the sequence and gameplay, not by assigning semantic names to burn-in digits.
self-test.note: The complete 19-position burn-in order agrees with the SDU decoder circuit. OPEN positions are swept too. A transition is not proof of physical fitment.

switch-test.note: Each isolated public 1-40 closure displays its own number. The six factory Not Used positions are included; ROM recognition does not establish a fitted contact. Three-second held snapshots decode the low seven segment bits; bit 0x80 is the comma. The earlier switch-test folder remained in the solenoid test and is retained for diagnosis only; switch-test-v2 is the accepted sweep.
